findings.location: Purity test of M1, used by B12-B15 (the not-text_regex marker list), and the B12-B15 gap '14 of 14 sampled texts were pure'
findings.claim: The only-content test sends to B15x every amendment whose text also gives status to persons, directs how incumbents are treated, or states a further effect. B12-B15 hold only pure amendments.
findings.evidence: The marker regex misses singular and variant wordings. These B14 members are decided `no` (merged_into_parent_on_issue) even though their held text has a further operative provision of the same kind the doctrine sends to B15x (EO 3303, 5775): EO 6047 'The present incumbent of this position is included in the classified service with the position'; EO 5817 'are hereby included, with their incumbents, in the classified competitive service'; EO 5901 'The effect of this amendment will be to include the position of one assistant with its incumbent in the classified competitive service'; EO 4720 'The effect of the above amendment is to bring the positions named with their present occupants within the competitive classified service'; EO 4948 'Those Indians now in the service ... may ... be treated as classified', plus freestanding reinstatement and first-grade-status provisions; EO 2780 'shall not be construed to require any person now holding the office of shipping commissioner to pass an examination in order to retain such office'; EO 4221 'Special agents so employed shall be continued in office, without examination, so long as their services are efficient'. Separately, EO 1451's operative text ('Hereafter paragraphs (a) and (b) of section 1 of Civil Rule VII shall apply to the appointment of rural carriers ... No inquiry shall be made as to the political or religious opinions') has no amending words. It passes prong 2 only because the Wikisource title and apparatus say 'Amending'.
findings.fix: Widen the marker list, for example: present incumbent(s)?|present occupants|with (its|their) (present )?(incumbents?|occupants)|effect of (this|the above|the foregoing) (order|amendment)|now holding|now in the service|shall be continued in office|be treated as classified. Run the amending-word test on the operative body, with Wikisource and Richardson headers stripped. Move EO 2780, 4221, 4720, 4948, 5817, 5901 and 6047 to B15x and EO 1451 to B18. Restate the B12-B15 count (391 becomes at most 383) and the totals. Replace the '14 of 14 sampled texts were pure' gap with the observed leak rate.

findings.location: .md 'Terms used', Schedule A and Schedule B
findings.claim: Schedules A and B were 'Lists that formed part of the rules from 1903'.
findings.evidence: EO 209 as promulgated (held Wikisource text) contains only Schedule A. Its notes say a part of it was 'Later replaced by an entire Schedule B by Executive Order 1180, March 23, 1910'. The EO 1180 text adds '(b) appointment to the positions named in Schedule B of these rules', and its WPA summary reads 'new Schedule B ... now prescribed'.
findings.fix: Schedule A formed part of the rules from 1903. Schedule B (positions filled by noncompetitive examination) was added by EO 1180 of March 23, 1910.

summary: The doctrine's structure follows the coordinator rulings. Ruling P2 governs pure amendments; EO 89's 'revokes all others' and EO 209's 'in lieu of those promulgated May 6, 1896, and the amendments thereof' are correctly treated as express class ends; EO 209 is correctly held open under P3; savings clauses are not treated as ends. All held pins and FR, Stat. and CFR citations check out against the held texts, except for a soft-hyphen pin mismatch in S4. Four errors need fixing. (1) B01 dates EO 89's end at 1903-03-20, the signing date of EO 209, instead of its stated effective date 1903-04-15. (2) The order that superseded EO 3807 is EO 5459, not EO 5495, which is a Wyoming public water reserve. (3) The purity test leaks: at least seven B14 members carry incumbent or status provisions of the same kind the doctrine sends to B15x (EO 2780, 4221, 4720, 4948, 5817, 5901, 6047), and EO 1451 passes only on Wikisource title words; all eight are wrongly decided `no`. (4) The .md reports one contradiction flag, but the engine reports 37; EO 119 alone has 15 later amendment edges besides the EO 12680 OCR splits. Minor issues: the B13 and B14 date windows overlap; Schedule B dates from 1910 (EO 1180), not 1903; the two B06 members are readable one-person waivers, not unread scans; the stated reason EO 5657 is open is wrong. The open list is otherwise honest. No `yes` lead is proposed.
